data.title: SpaceX Stock Price Forecast: Goldman Sachs Reaps Another SpaceX Windfall as Wall Street Sees 49% Upside
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) stock rose more than 6% in Friday's trading to $157.53. Wall Street analysts see 49% upside from that level. The stock's move comes as Bloomberg reports that Goldman Sachs (GS) has earned hundreds of millions of dollars from wealthy clients who invested in SpaceX years before its IPO. The bank helped arrange those investments when SpaceX was valued at tens of billions of dollars.

Goldman Sachs Earns More From Early SpaceX Bets

Goldman Sachs helped wealthy clients invest in SpaceX more than five years ago, when the company was still private. At the time, SpaceX was valued at tens of billions of dollars, far below the valuation it reached when it went public.

SpaceX priced its IPO at $135 per share in June. The company offered 555.6 million shares and raised about $75 billion. The IPO valued SpaceX at about $1.77 trillion.

Promotion

High conviction on SPCX? Try Tradr's SPCM or SPCG

Bloomberg reported Friday that some of Goldman's clients have since sold SpaceX shares and realized large gains. Goldman received incentive fees tied to those gains, according to people familiar with the matter. The fees have reached hundreds of millions of dollars.

The fees from those early investments are separate from Goldman's IPO underwriting fees. Goldman and Morgan Stanley each received about $100 million from the SpaceX IPO's underwriting fees, according to reports.

SpaceX Gives Early Investors a Chance to Cash In

SpaceX's public listing has given early investors a way to realize gains from stakes they acquired when the company was worth far less.

The Goldman report shows how valuable those early investments became after SpaceX reached a $1.77 trillion valuation. It also shows the range of fees available to banks that helped wealthy clients access private companies before they reached public markets.

Goldman has now earned fees at both ends of the SpaceX journey — from helping clients invest early and from the IPO.

What Is SPCX's Stock Price Target?

SPCX stock has a Strong Buy consensus rating on TipRanks based on 27 Buys, four Holds, and two Sells assigned in the last three months. The average price target for SpaceX is $235.10 implying an upside of 49% from the current price.

data.title: Neocloud Stocks CoreWeave, Nebius, and Iren Are Rising Today, Oct. 2 — Here's Why
data.description:
Shares in neocloud companies CoreWeave (CRWV), Nebius (NBIS), and IREN Limited (IREN) traded higher on Friday morning. This follows positive company-specific updates relating to CoreWeave and Nebius. Nebius led the rally, rising by over 5% to about $244 per share.

Cantor Fitzgerald Stays Bullish on CoreWeave over Improving Profits

On Friday, Cantor Fitzgerald's five-star analyst Brett Knoblauch reaffirmed his Buy rating on CoreWeave's shares. He also set a price target of $176. This suggests nearly 100% upside from Thursday's closing price of $88.57.

Defending the rating, Knoblauch pointed out that CoreWeave has raised its GPU price twice this year: by 25% in July and an additional 10% afterward. He expects these price changes to boost CoreWeave's earnings in 2027 and especially 2028.

Promotion

CWVX: an alternative to margin or options on CRWV

The analyst argued that this boost will build on CoreWeave's already-improving profit margins.

"From a financial perspective, CoreWeave stated they have 10x demand for every megawatt of capacity," noted Knoblauch.

He explained further: "They [CoreWeave] remained extremely confident in hitting their 8 GW target by the end of the decade, with the company seemingly focused on adding international capacity at the request of customers, while also emphasizing a greater mix of self-builds going forward."

Nebius Expands with Inferize Acquisition

Meanwhile, the rally in Nebius shares comes a day after the Amsterdam-based company announced its acquisition of Inferize.

Inferize provides the technology that helps companies shorten the time it takes to launch and expand large AI models. Nebius expects this tech to help strengthen its Token Factory

The Nebius Token Factory is a platform designed for AI inference. This refers to running AI models for tasks such as responding to user queries. Nebius expects Inferize tech to help it use its GPU capacity more efficiently.

"Cold starts — the time models need to load before serving a single request — impose additional time and costs on teams running AI models in production at scale," Nebius noted. Inferize's tech helps to close this gap, the company noted.

Of the three neocloud stocks mentioned in this article, only IREN Limited (IREN) currently carries a Strong Buy consensus rating from analysts. In addition, TipRanks' Stock Comparison tool shows that IREN leads the group with about 87% upside.

The upside is based on the average IREN price target of $77.36.

data.title: Seagate vs. Western Digital: One Stock Is a Buy After Today's Drop, but the Other Has More Upside, According to Goldman Sachs
data.description:
Seagate Technology (NASDAQ:STX) and Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) are getting hammered Friday, with both stocks tumbling around 13% during the session. The selloff follows reports that Toshiba plans to double its hard-disk-drive production capacity by fiscal 2027, raising concerns that one of the biggest advantages enjoyed by Seagate and Western Digital – tight industry supply – could eventually begin to fade. Toshiba plans to invest roughly ¥60 billion, or about $380 million, in the expansion and wants to increase its share of HDD capacity from just over 10% toward 30% over the medium term.

That prospect is particularly uncomfortable after a huge run for both stocks. AI data centers have created heavy demand for high-capacity storage, while limited supply has helped HDD manufacturers raise prices and improve profitability. More Toshiba capacity could eventually challenge that favorable balance, although the expansion will take time and analysts have questioned how much the competitive landscape will actually change.

Goldman Prefers Seagate

Against that backdrop, Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider, who ranks among the top 3% of Wall Street analysts, sees a strong case for owning Seagate.

Promotion

Double your STX exposure with Tradr's STXX

Schneider believes Seagate can deliver outsized earnings growth over the coming year, helped by strong incremental margins and the rollout of its heat-assisted magnetic recording, or HAMR, technology. Higher earnings could also leave the company with more room to return capital as it pays down its remaining debt.

"We would be buyers of the stock, especially in light of the recent pullback," the analyst said, arguing that Seagate should remain a key winner from tight industry conditions and strong pricing.

Schneider backs that call with a Buy rating and a $960 price target, which points to ~17% upside for STX.

Schneider's view is largely in step with the rest of Wall Street. Seagate carries a Strong Buy consensus rating, with 14 of 16 analysts recommending the stock and the other two saying Hold. The $1,080.13 average price target implies about 31% upside from current levels. (See STX stock forecast)

data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Advances as Jobs Report Miss Sends Rate Hike Odds Lower
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is up 0.42% on Friday after a weak jobs report sent rate hike odds lower. In September, the U.S. economy added 29,000 nonfarm payrolls, well below the estimate of 84,000. Private payrolls rose by 46,000, while government employment fell by 17,000. Furthermore, the unemployment rate increased to 4.2% from 4.1%, topping expectations of 4.1%. The rate rose to 4.18% from 4.14% on an unrounded basis.

Following the report, the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the October 28 Fed meeting dipped to 21.6% from 24.4% on Thursday and 64.2% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool. In addition, the odds of unchanged rates rose to 78.4% from 75.6% a day ago and 35.8% a week ago.

Steady rates are generally viewed as more accretive to stocks than higher rates. Lower, rather than higher, rates allow companies to borrow capital more easily and can encourage hiring. In addition, lower rates increase the present value of discounted future cash flows.

data.title: Bitcoin Futures Positions Surge by $2.3 Billion as Traders Pay Top Dollar for Upward Bets
data.description:
Derivatives market data shows trader activity picking up across crypto exchanges. Bitcoin's (BTC-USD) open interest grew by roughly 27,000 BTC, rising from 626,000 BTC on September 30 to 653,000 BTC. This change brought total market value in unsettled BTC contracts to $56.2 billion, marking a 4.3% jump in total position value.

During that same time frame, Bitcoin prices rose from $83,500 to $85,520. When Bitcoin's open interest expands while BTC prices rise, new trades are entering the market to support the current price path. Total open interest at the end of September for Bitcoin had hovered near 12-month low points, meaning this new BTC price jump starts from a lower base.
data.author: Annika Masrani

data.title: Paramount Skydance Stock (PSKY) Rises as CEO David Ellison Reveals Name Change Plans
data.description:
Paramount Skydance (PSKY) stock was up 0.59% on Friday after the entertainment company's CEO commented on plans for a name change. CEO David Ellison said that he plans to change the company's name after it completes its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). This would see the new company operate under the name "Skydance."

Ellison revealed the name change in an X post on Friday. He said, "Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling."

Ellison said that he decided to change the name of the combined company for a couple of reasons. He said the first goal of the change was to preserve the identity of each of these companies. By adopting the name Skydance, it shows the dedication to not let Paramount or Warner Bros. Discovery overshadow each other.

data.title: Cerebras Gets Buy Upgrade as Analyst Calls 17% Selloff an Overreaction
data.description:
AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems (CBRS) was upgraded to Buy from Hold by Freedom Capital Markets after its shares fell by about 17% on concerns that key customer OpenAI is using Nvidia (NVDA) hardware for part of its newest AI model. Analyst Paul Meeks set a $209 price target and argued that investors may be overreacting because demand for AI computing still exceeds available supply. He also believes that Cerebras remains well positioned as AI workloads shift toward faster inference.

The selloff followed reports that OpenAI is using AI chip giant Nvidia's GPUs for the Ultrafast version of its GPT-1 Sol model. That raised fears that Cerebras could lose business from one of its most important partners.

However, Meeks believes that OpenAI will continue using several types of chips because no single supplier can meet every AI workload.

Promotion

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on CBRS

That view is supported by OpenAI's existing deal with Cerebras. In January, OpenAI agreed to add 750 megawatts of Cerebras computing capacity to its platform, with the systems scheduled to come online in stages through 2028. OpenAI said at the time that Cerebras would provide dedicated low-latency inference capacity.

Cerebras Is Still Adding New Inference Customers

It's also worth noting that Cerebras signed another major infrastructure agreement this week. Cloud startup Gimlet Labs plans to deploy roughly 100 megawatts of Cerebras hardware for AI inference. Cerebras will provide its CS-4 systems over the next one to two years, and Gimlet expects to make the hardware available through its cloud in 2027.

That deal supports Freedom's argument that inference could remain a major growth opportunity even if customers continue buying Nvidia GPUs. Meeks also sees a possible future where different chips handle different parts of the same AI request.

For example, Nvidia GPUs could handle the first stage where a model processes a user's prompt, and Cerebras hardware could then handle the stage where the model generates its response.

That approach could let Cerebras compete with Nvidia on some workloads while still working alongside Nvidia hardware on others.

data.title: "A Feature We Hope You Never Need": Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Surges After "Emergency Drive Away" Arrives
data.description:
It is an interesting idea, creating a feature that you hope never gets used. Electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA) recently did just that with its new "Emergency Drive Away," that made it to a recent over-the-air update, according to a report from Business Insider. The news caught investors' attention, and shares jumped over 5% in Friday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 17.62% loss in its share price over the past year.

A Lot Like Insurance, Really

The emergency drive away feature offers a surprising tool that is, as the name suggests, meant to be used in the even of an emergency. It allows users to shift quickly into drive while plugged into a Supercharger station. Normally, that does not happen, and for the most part, it should not. Driving away with a Supercharger cable plugged into the car would be a disaster. But sometimes, it is necessary; just ask Dale Schultz, survivor of a shooting near an In-N-Out in Twin Falls, Idaho, who was charging his Tesla as the shooting commenced.

So while the possibility exists that this feature may be necessary someday, Tesla—via Max de Zegher, senior director of charging in North America—made it clear that this feature should almost never actually be used. He noted, "We select Supercharger locations with safety in mind and relocate sites deemed unsafe. Our goal is that you always feel safe getting out to unplug. We went back and forth on this for years, but believe offering it is the right call. Don't abuse it, so we don't have to restrict it."

Promotion

TSLQ: built for a short position on TSLA

A Different Reason for the Roadster Delay?

We know that the Roadster event got pushed back due to weather, and this got a lot of people thinking about the Roadster's potential ability to fly being part of its operation. And certainly, "high winds" would be a problem for any kind of flying car debut. But a report from Teslarati offered up a new possibility: what if the delay had nothing to do with flying?

The Roadster may never actually leave the ground, but still be impacted by wind. After all, the Roadster is unique, and could deliver some very exciting metrics, like its acceleration and top speed. The last thing Tesla would need here is to have its Roadster slowed by headwinds.
